deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a page of lecture or school notes on history and geography, probably not in Gauss's own hand; it may be a student's or family member's notebook kept with the bundle. It continues section 'VI. Afrikanische Völker' from the previous page.

Content, paraphrased:
(1) The ancients' knowledge of Africa came through the Carthaginians and Egyptians, and its sources were merchants. After Carthage ceased to exist, contact with the African interior continued.
(2) In the 7th century the Arabs penetrated Africa, spread their religion, reached the middle of the continent and have remained there to the present.
(3) Africa differs strikingly from Asia and Europe. It has a much more regular outline, which made discovery difficult. It has no gulfs reaching deep inland and lacks large rivers. As a result, vast deserts can form in which heat concentrates.
(4) The interior contains regions humans cannot explore, and great natural salt deposits ('Salzmagazine'). By far the largest part of Africa lies in the torrid zone.
(5) Africa was circumnavigated once in antiquity (the Phoenician voyage under Necho reported by Herodotus), but this had no further consequences.
(6) A new section begins: 'Geschichte von Ägypten. Kurze Uebersicht der Geographie von Aegypten'. Egypt is said to contain 2/3 of (the area of) Germany and to be 100 German miles long; the sentence continues on the next page.

There are no derivations, computations or problems to reconstruct. The only quantitative statements are the descriptive figures in (6).
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics.

Factual remark: 'Egypt = 2/3 of Germany' is only a rough contemporary estimate. Modern Egypt (~1.0 million km²) is larger than the German Confederation of 1815 (~630,000 km²). The figure presumably refers to a narrower notion of Egypt (the Nile land up to the cataracts), so it is not a computational error.
Calling Africa's interior a land 'man cannot discover' reflects the state of European knowledge around 1816.

results.what: Descriptive historical-geographical notes on Africa (Arab expansion, coastline regularity, deserts, torrid zone, ancient circumnavigation) and the start of a geography of Egypt (area about 2/3 of Germany, length 100 German miles).
results.modern_name: None (school or lecture notes in history/geography, non-mathematical)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard textbook content of the period (e.g. in the tradition of Heeren's or Gatterer's universal history and geography)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is non-mathematical history/geography notes, likely not even written by Gauss. It contains nothing of mathematical or Gauss-specific interest.

checkable.asserts: Two-thirds of the area of the German Confederation (~630,000 km²) is about 420,000 km², the area the note implicitly assigns to Egypt.
100 German (geographic) miles of about 7.42 km each come to about 742 km, the stated length of Egypt.
